tools.name: zvec_grep_callees
tools.description: Outgoing call sites for a symbol. Shows callee definitions and call-site locations in the caller file. Accepts name, scope::name or scope.name; ::name selects top-level definitions. Queries matching more than 10 indexed definitions fail; narrow the scope or use globs. limit counts call sites per definition (default 20, maximum 50); a truncation notice marks omitted sites. Exact misses may return suggestions without call sites. Returns readable text with one-based line and byte-column numbers. Requires graph indexing enabled with zg --index --graph (add --rebuild for an existing index). Reads persisted resolved calls without refreshing; empty results do not prove absence.

globs.description: Ordered workspace-relative glob rules for definitions and suggestions; call-site files remain unrestricted.

insensitiveGlobs.description: Ordered case-insensitive glob rules, applied after globs, as in search.

limit.description: Maximum call sites per matching symbol; defaults to 20, capped at 50.

search.instructions: Use the current workspace as evidence. Available zg tool: zvec_grep_search. Use search for conceptual discovery, unknown locations and synthesis of evidence across files; use native Grep or rg when exact lookup alone is sufficient. Pass an absolute root visible to the daemon. Creating or rebuilding an index requires user authorization. Respect declined or cancelled index setup. tools.name: zvec_grep_search
tools.description: Search a workspace index for conceptual and cross-file evidence such as architecture, source paths related to calls, dependencies, lifecycle, data or control flow, design rationale, and comparisons. This retrieves source evidence, not an exact call graph. Use it when exact lookup alone cannot answer a workspace-grounded question. Results start with freshness and any global index diagnostics, followed by CLI-formatted bounded source snippets; set preview: "full" to return each complete stored entity without changing retrieval or ranking. Treat sufficient returned content as already-read evidence without a status preflight. Use native Grep or rg instead when exact lookup alone is sufficient. A missing index can request user model selection and authorization; accepted setup starts a background build and returns indexing status. Retry after completion.

GlobListInput.description: Public string/list globs plus the existing typed-rule extension.

root.description: Absolute workspace root visible to the daemon.

queries.description: One or more primary hybrid-search groups.

limit.description: Maximum returned items per query group or fused plan.

preview.description: CLI source display: short bounds snippets; full returns each complete stored entity without changing retrieval or ranking. Freshness precedes results.

globs.description: Ordered path glob rules; later matching rules take precedence.

insensitiveGlobs.description: Ordered case-insensitive rg glob rules, applied after globs.

fileTypes.description: Ripgrep type names, such as ts, py, h or cpp.

includedFormats.description: Formats inferred from indexed file names, such as rust or markdown; source contents are not inspected.

excludedFormats.description: Exclude matching file-name formats, taking precedence over included formats.

categories.description: Categories inferred from indexed file names, such as code or document.

excludedCategories.description: Exclude matching file-name categories, taking precedence over categories.

embeddingConcurrency.description:
Index-only refresh concurrency. ORT direct mode sets the session count. In server mode, limits this operation's session use within the startup-configured pool; omitted uses pool capacity. Queries share the pool with their own limit.
Must be positive. ORT caps requests above pool capacity; it never resizes server pools or changes their shared CPU thread budget.

fuse.description: Collapse all query groups into one ranked plan.

symbolTypes.description: Restrict indexed results to symbol types.

modifiedAfter.description: Only query files modified after this time.

modifiedBefore.description: Only query files modified before this time.

freshness.description:
Search now or wait for delivered workspace changes to be indexed.
Resident servers cover watcher notifications received before the refresh
barrier; OS notifications delivered later require a subsequent refresh.

autoUpdate.description: Allow eventual search to schedule a background index update.
